author: Bobby Grayson
description: elixir/to_lean.exs fallthrough/5 now returns {rhs, ctx, deferred}. When no later clause of the same module is at least as general: if cl.mod in ctx.defers the fallback is '(sp, [.send me <msg_name>])' and deferred=true, else the old behaviour (warning 'clause i guard has no fallthrough; Elixir would crash, modelled as no-op' and '(sp, [])'). In render_clauses/2 a deferred clause names the whole message with an as-pattern msg_name(env)@(mp) and forces the self name to 'me' (self_name(env) might be '_'). msg_name/1 picks m' when the clause already binds a variable m. This matches BEAM semantics: a receive arm whose guard fails does not consume the message. Verified by the builder only on an uncommitted scratch module (no committed example exercises a guarded receive clause).
title: Guard failure in a defer module: a guarded receive clause with no more-general later clause re-enqueues instead of the GenServer no-op; fallthrough/5 returns deferred=true, header becomes '| me, _, sp, m@(.pat)' (m' if the clause binds m), and no 'guard has no fallthrough' warning is emitted
